summary.headline: Schaeffler India Q2 CY26 revenue rose 17.5% YoY to INR 2,681 crore, with EBITDA of INR 513 crore at a 19.1% margin.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 17.5% YoY and 7% QoQ to INR 2,681 crore, led by Automotive Technologies (+33% YoY) and exports (+24%). EBITDA rose 14.3% YoY to INR 513 crore at 19.1% margin, and PAT was about INR 337 crore versus INR 320 crore a year earlier. Working capital rose to INR 2,029 crore on planned inventory build, which pressured free cash flow. Management flagged input cost pressure (LPG, propane, freight, wages under new Labour Codes) that is not yet recovered from customers, with price-indexation recoveries expected in H2.

financial_highlights.change: H1 EBIT margin 15.8%; H1 PAT margin ~12.6-12.7%

segments.name: Automotive Technologies (~35% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew 33% YoY and 3.6% QoQ; conventional ICE business up ~20% YoY and e-mobility drove the rest. Management said PV market fell ~8% QoQ while the company's business grew 3.6%, implying share gains.

segments.name: Bearings and Industrial Solutions (~35% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew ~5% YoY and 6.5% QoQ. Non-mobility industrial reportedly grew double digits, while automotive bearings were sluggish, and wind energy saw a revenue dip from contract negotiations.

segments.name: Vehicle Lifetime Solutions (~12% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew 9.9% YoY and double digits QoQ; growth constrained by Hosur capacity, with OEMs prioritised over aftermarket.

segments.name: Exports (~17% of revenue)
segments.commentary: Grew 24% YoY; H1 growth about 28% YoY, driven mainly by intercompany allocations from Savli capacity.

segments.name: KRSV (Koovers), wholly owned subsidiary
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 79 crore in quarter, EBITDA still negative; management targets EBITDA and cash breakeven in 2029, with a sales cut-off adjustment of INR 5.6 crore and ~INR 3 crore founders' bonus provision.

guidance_outlook: Export growth target ~15-20% stated as aspiration; management said it never guided growth, and it wants exports capped near 20% of total. Guidance is being kept careful given geopolitics.
H2 FY27 expected to recover lost free-cash-flow ground as working capital normalises; inventory build described as planned.
FX indexation price corrections with OEMs expected in H2; steel indexation also expected to give traction.
Management says wage-cost increases (~10% average) and fuel/freight costs are not expected to be recovered from customers and will be absorbed through productivity (VA/VE).

CY26 capex of INR 400-500 crore: about INR 175 crore spent in H1, remaining ~INR 250-300 crore to be spent in H2 (INR 120 crore automotive, INR 170 crore Automotive Technologies, balance B&IS per the CFO's split). Sustaining capex ~10% of total.
Aspiration to return B&IS and industrial business to double-digit growth; no timeline given.
capex_capacity: CY26 capex plan INR 400-500 crore; about INR 175 crore spent in H1 and orders placed for machinery for capacity and localisation.
Capex split for the remainder: close to INR 120 crore automotive, INR 170 crore Automotive Technologies, rest B&IS.
Hosur plant capacity constraint is limiting VLS supply; management is adding capacity and developing local suppliers.
Export growth driven by Savli (India) capacity built for localisation and used for group intercompany supply.
Sustaining capex is roughly 10% of total capex.
demand_pricing: Auto production: PV output fell ~8% QoQ in June, yet company's PV business grew 3.6% QoQ against a market decline. Two-wheeler and commercial vehicle output strong; PV production up 15.7% YoY.
Tractor demand and double-clutch adoption cited as a win; monsoon performance flagged as a watch item.
Input costs up: LPG and propane (West Asia), freight (air freight used for Hosur VLS material), fuel. Other expenses rose to 15.4% of revenue from 15.1% a year ago.
Automotive OEM pricing uses indexation for some commodities; LPG, propane and wage costs are not on the indexation list, so recovery is under negotiation.
Intercompany exports priced at arm's length with a year-end true-up in December under OECD guidelines.

Bearings and Industrial: wins in cylindrical roller bearings, DGBBs, spherical rollers, TRBs and plain bearings; raw material and steel/cement/aluminium sectors grew strongly. Railways is tender-based and slow.

qa_highlights.question: Why is industrial growth soft at ~5% YoY, how much revenue was consciously let go, and when will B&IS return to double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited strong raw-material and power transmission growth (~8%), with wind energy hit by timing and global contract negotiations. Railways is tender-based. Aim is double-digit growth, but no timeline or revenue-loss figure was given.

qa_highlights.question: What is driving export growth well above the ~10-12% FY26 guidance, and will it be revised?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said it is mainly intercompany allocation from localised Savli capacity, with double-digit demand across regions and rupee/USD billing benefits. Order book is solid, but guidance will be cautious; the ~20% figure is a cap on exports as a share of total, not a growth target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is aftermarket (VLS) growth slowing to ~10% from over 20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capacity constraints led to OEM prioritisation over VLS. Capacity additions and local supplier development are in progress.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pass-through mechanism and why did gross margin expand?
qa_highlights.answer: Auto OEM pricing is index-based for some commodities; LPG, propane and wage costs are not indexed. Recovery is expected in H2 via FX and steel indexation. Management declined to split pricing across segments.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Koovers' EBITDA margin worsen from 13.4% to 17.3% and when is breakeven?
qa_highlights.answer: Sales cut-off accounting adjustment of INR 5.6 crore and a ~INR 3 crore founders' bonus provision. EBITDA and cash breakeven expected in 2029.

qa_highlights.question: What drove Automotive Technologies' 31-33% growth, and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Conventional ICE business grew ~20% YoY and e-mobility contributed the rest, with timing differences. Management said the growth reflects market-share gains against a ~8% PV market decline rather than content per vehicle.

qa_highlights.question: What is the remaining CY26 capex and its split?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 500 crore is to be consumed in the remainder of CY26, including orders placed. Split: ~INR 120 crore automotive, ~INR 170 crore Automotive Technologies, rest B&IS. Sustaining capex is ~10% of the total.

risks_watch: Working capital at INR 2,029 crore and weaker free cash flow; recovery depends on H2 inventory unwind.
Input cost and freight pressure (LPG, propane, fuel, wage codes at ~10% wage increase) may not be recovered from customers; management plans to absorb through productivity.
Weak automotive bearings business, which management describes as commoditised and under pressure; cost-competitiveness and localisation actions pending.
Monsoon and tractor demand, and PV production volatility.
Export sustainability and FX dependence; management is cautious on guidance due to geopolitical disruption.
KRSV (Koovers) still loss-making, with EBITDA breakeven now targeted for 2029.
Wind energy contract negotiations and tender-based railway demand.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and market-share momentum, but cautious on margins, free cash flow and export guidance. Management was evasive on segment pricing and on the timing of B&IS and automotive bearings recovery.
key_quotes: Quarter 2 has been a very strong performance and recognitions coming from the customer side as well.
Free cash flow certainly is under focus, and we have work to do here as well.
We will be careful in future guidance due to the ongoing geopolitical disruptions.
It is very unlikely that the customer will reimburse, this customer would expect that we are doing some productivity measures, VA/VE, etcetera, to absorb such kind of cost.

adds.what: CY26 capex INR 400-500 crore incl. machinery orders for capacity and localisation (not individually quantified)

growth.why: Management sustains export growth of about 15-20% (an aspiration it said it never formally guided) and CY26 capex of INR 400-500 crore with about INR 250-300 crore still to be spent in H2, backed by capacity and localisation machinery orders, Savli export capacity and price-indexation recoveries expected in H2; Hosur capacity constraint is limiting VLS growth.
